newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday on a technical correction after sharp gains early this week, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.70 percent from 13.20 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover rose to 7.06 million lots from 5.99 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the rates were likely to recover on Friday and early next week due to more new domestic A share issues, which would attract more funds from the repo market.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed and traders said they were likely to have a technical rebound in the next few trading days after three weeks of falls.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006 ended down at 119.75 yuan from 120.41 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.06 million lots from 913,090 lots.
"Some financial institutions began to build positions today after the downward trend since the start of this month," a local trader said. "A technical rebound is likely in the short term."
